chunks.subject: science
chunks.text: Microorganisms are tiny living things. They are too small to be seen clearly with the naked eye. Examples of microorganisms include bacteria, fungi, protozoa, and some algae. Some microorganisms are useful. For example, bacteria can help make yogurt and bread production can involve yeast. Some microorganisms are harmful. They can spoil food or cause disease. Students should understand: 1. microorganisms are tiny living things 2. not all microorganisms are harmful 3. some microorganisms are useful in daily life

chunks.subject: science
chunks.text: Microorganisms are tiny living things. They are so small that we cannot see them clearly with our eyes. Examples of microorganisms include bacteria, fungi, and yeast. Some microorganisms are useful, such as bacteria used to make yogurt. Some microorganisms are harmful and can cause diseases. Microorganisms can spread through air, water, or food.
